newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian GDP rose 0.7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italian GDP rose 0.7 pct in 1996.

text.p: Italy's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose a final 0.7 percent in 1996, the national statistics institute ISTAT said on Friday.

Its statistics on the state of the economy said the rise compared with 2.9 percent GDP growth in 1995, revised down from a previous 3.0 percent. ISTAT also revised the 1994 GDP figure to an increase of 2.2 percent from a previous 2.1 percent.
ISTAT said exports by volume fell 0.3 percent in 1996 after a rise of 11.6 percent in 1995. Imports by volume fell 2.6 percent last year following a rise of 9.6 percent in 1995.
Internal consumption in 1996 rose by 0.7 percent compared with a 1.1 percent rise in 1995, the institute said.
Exports in terms of value rose 1.7 percent in 1996 after a 23.0 percent climb the year before, while the value of imports fell 4.4 percent also following a 23.0 percent increase in 1995.
Istat said that 1996 GDP was boosted by a 2.4 percent rise in the agriculture sector and a 1.8 percent increase in the construction sector.
The industry sector saw a 0.4 percent fall and energy fell 0.7 percent.
In its overview of the economy, Istat said employment rose 0.2 percent last year -- the first time the job total had increased for four years.
And the statistics office confirmed that the ratio between Italy's budget deficit and GDP was 6.7 percent last year from 7.0 percent the year before.
Stripping interest payments out of the equation, Italy had a primary surplus of 4.0 percent in 1996. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
